hello.note: Guten Tag (GOO-ten TAHK) is the polite daytime greeting. In the South you also hear Grüß Gott (grews GOT)

good-morning.note: Used until about 10 or 11 in the morning

good-night.note: Only at bedtime or when parting late. To greet someone in the evening, say guten Abend (GOO-ten AH-bent)

please.note: Bitte also means you're welcome and here you are

thank-you.note: Danke schön (shurn) and vielen Dank (FEE-len dahnk) mean thank you very much

excuse-me.note: Also means sorry. Verzeihung (fair-TSY-oong) is more formal

my-name.note: Mein Name ist... also works. The audio uses Peter as the example name

dont-understand.note: The ch is a soft hiss made at the front of the mouth

how-much.note: Wie viel kostet das? (vee feel) is also common

would-like.note: The polite way to order. The audio uses einen Kaffee as the example

i-want.note: The standard polite I'd like. Ich will (want) is blunt. The audio uses das hier (this one) as the example

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses Wasser (water) as the example

discount.text: Können Sie mir einen besseren Preis machen?
discount.say: KUR-nen zee meer EYE-nen BES-er-en pryss MAH-khen
discount.note: Haggling is unusual in Germany; try only at flea markets

card.note: Many small shops and cafés take only cash, so it is worth asking

bill.note: Zahlen, bitte (TSAH-len) is the short version in restaurants

checkout-time.text: Um wie viel Uhr ist der Check-out?
checkout-time.say: oom vee feel oor ist dair CHEK-owt

wifi.note: Germans say WLAN (VEE-lahn) rather than wifi

taxi.text: Können Sie mir ein Taxi rufen?
taxi.say: KUR-nen zee meer yne TAHK-see ROO-fen

bus-station.note: Often shown as ZOB, the central bus station

train-station.note: The main station is the Hauptbahnhof (HOWPT-bahn-hohf), written Hbf

which-train.note: Swap in any city; the audio uses Hanoi as the example

buy-ticket.text: Wo kann ich eine Fahrkarte kaufen?
buy-ticket.say: voh kahn ikh EYE-nuh FAR-kar-tuh KOW-fen
buy-ticket.note: Fahrkarte means ticket; Ticket also works

two-tickets.text: Kann ich zwei Fahrkarten nach... kaufen?
two-tickets.say: kahn ikh tsvy FAR-kar-ten nahkh ... KOW-fen
two-tickets.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
two-tickets.spoken: Kann ich zwei Fahrkarten nach Hanoi kaufen?

trip-length.text: Wie lange dauert die Fahrt nach...?
trip-length.say: vee LAHNG-uh DOW-ert dee FAHRT nahkh ...
trip-length.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
trip-length.spoken: Wie lange dauert die Fahrt nach Hanoi?

delicious.note: Lecker (LEK-er) is the everyday word for tasty

allergic.note: Add the food: Nüsse (nuts), Eier (eggs), Meeresfrüchte (seafood). The audio uses Nüsse as the example

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: Einen Tisch für zwei Personen, bitte
table-for-two.say: EYE-nen tish fewr tsvy pair-ZOH-nen BIT-uh
table-for-two.note: For more people use drei (3) or vier (4) instead of zwei

beer.note: Ein Bier vom Fass (fahs) is a draught beer

coffee.note: Ein Kaffee is filter coffee. Ask for einen Espresso or einen Milchkaffee for the other kinds

water.note: Ask for stilles Wasser (SHTIL-es) for still, or mit Kohlensäure (koh-len-ZOY-ruh) for sparkling

milk.note: The ch is a soft hiss

cheers.note: Look people in the eye as you clink glasses

help.note: Shout it. The police are die Polizei (dee po-lee-TSY)
